part.Name: Description
part.Short: Road-worn and rumor-led, they carry everything they own: a bedroll, an empty skin, and the name of a place where thirst is shared.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Dust of a dozen roads on their boots, and no bedroll unpacked. They are only stopping.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Carries themselves like someone with somewhere better to be, and one good reason not to be there yet.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Lashed poles and borrowed planks. Somebody's promise is being kept, plank by plank.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Casks in a cradle of watervine rope. The whole settlement is counted here, dram by dram.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Watervine trained up a frame of lashed poles, tended for its own sake now rather than the settlement's. Whoever lives here eats a little better for the bother.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Stretched hides scraped and staked to cure in the sun. The household has taken up tanning, and the smell has followed them home.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A cask of dreadroot and iron-salt liquor, stirred with a paddle gone the colour of the dye. What comes out of it rides with the caravans.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Scraped skins pinned flat under a weighted board until they lie true enough to write on. Somebody here reads, and somebody here teaches it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A tin-lined belly sunk to its rim in the earth. It makes nothing: what is in it was carried here in somebody's arms or run down a gutter from the works above. When it is full, the whole town sleeps easier; when it rings hollow, everyone hears it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A communal chest with a slatted lid, cool air moving through the gaps. What is put in here feeds the settlement, not just whoever finds it first.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A patch of turned earth, staked and weeded by hands that have somewhere else to be. What comes up depends on what the ground already knew how to grow, long before anyone asked it to.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Canvas over a brinestalk frame, pegged against a wind that has opinions. It is not much. It is up before dark, which is the whole argument for it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Four tents in a line with a woven brake along the weather side. Nobody calls this a house, and everybody sleeps better.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Posts, wattle, and a door that shuts. The first building here that will still be standing when the person who raised it is not.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The hut, and a swept square of packed earth outside it with a rope line and a stool. Where the work happens when the weather allows it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Fieldstone to the eaves, timber above, and a hearth that draws properly. Two families and a cat.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Three households around one square, and a well-worn argument about whose turn it is to sweep it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A whole street raised in one season, every door the same width. The masons stopped signing them halfway along.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Marble facing over honest stone, and a step nobody is allowed to sit on. Somebody of consequence is expected, and will not arrive until the plaster is dry.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A courtyard, a gate that closes, and a name cut over the arch. Whether the name deserves the arch is the kind of thing the chronicle argues about for a hundred years.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Four storeys around a shaded well, stairs on the outside, washing on every rail. A quarter of the city roofed in one go, and full before the scaffolding came down.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A shallow bed scraped level and flooded thin. The sun takes the water and leaves something worth raking up; what drips off the drying racks at dusk is worth more still.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Pans stepped down a slope so each one drinks the last one's leavings. Worked in shifts by people who stopped noticing the smell some time ago.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Stretched canvas, a gutter of split cane, and a cask underneath. Nothing falls here; what it catches is the night giving back what the day took, and it works best when the cold is worst.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A whole roofline turned to the purpose, gutters running to a sunken row of casks. On a cold clear night it fills faster than the settlement drinks.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Squat domes of dressed stone, windowed on every face so the air walks through them, ranked around a sunken basin. They are cold inside at dawn and the walls run with it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Rank on rank of them out past the wall, spaced by a mason who worked out how far apart they had to stand, and gutters cut between the ranks to bring it all downhill to one place.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Somebody followed a damp seam back into the rock and found the lichen it was coming off. The face is cased in stone now, with a lead gutter under it and a cask at the end of that, and one of them goes down twice a day to scrape the growth back off the cut.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A worked gallery along the whole wet seam, propped and drained, with taps every few paces and a walkway that stays slick no matter what is laid on it. The lichen is farmed now rather than fought.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A hall built around one cold face, shuttered by day and thrown open at dusk, with the whole roof turned to catching what the stone gives up. The keepers took a dead still apart to learn it and never put that one back together.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stone lid over seven hundred drams and a hatch with a lock everybody has the key to. Cool enough down there to keep a body from going off, which has been tried.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Open water inside your own wall, lined with dressed stone and edged with a low kerb. Every dram in it was carried or channelled here by somebody; it is a held thing, not a found one. Children are told not to, and do anyway.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cistern, court, and channel, all one thing, and a keeper whose entire trade is knowing which valve. It makes not one dram: everything that goes through it came off the works upcountry or out of somebody's arms. The founder was elsewhere the day it was finished, and the chronicle says so in both registers.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Staked rows, weeded on a rota, watered by whoever drew the short straw. It is somebody's whole day and it feeds nine.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Turned earth to the fence line, sown by everyone who could be spared and harvested the same way. For two weeks of the year the settlement does nothing else.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Rows to the edge of the claim, and a plough that took a season's salvage to put together. The chronicle dates the good years from here.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Raised on staddle stones with a lid that keeps the vermin honest. What is in here is the difference between a bad year and a bad story.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Fields to the fence line, a threshing floor swept between harvests, and a barn at the end of them with the year's account chalked on the door. Three people work it and a whole town eats out of it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The quarter the rest of the city eats out of: rows past the eye's patience, a mill with metal in its gearing, and granaries standing in a line with their own road to the doors. It is the only paved way in the city that goes nowhere but a barn.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A whetstone, a tar pot, and a bench somebody keeps tidy without ever having been asked to. The camp's entire industry, and not nothing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A hearth, a hammer, and someone who walked a long way for the chance to swing it. The ring of it carries further than the wall does.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Banked overnight and never quite cold. Getting heat to stay put is harder than getting it to start, and this is the building that knows the difference.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A pit, two trestles, and timber stacked in ranks to season. One of them stands in the hole all day and gets the worse half of it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bankers, chisels, and a spoil heap that grows all summer. The heap is half of every block the settlement builds with.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A furnace, a crucible, and somebody who can read the colour of the melt. Getting scrap back to liquid is the easy half.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two stones and a long handle, and a fine grey dust on everything within ten paces. Turns a harvest into something that keeps.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Benches down both walls, everything hung where it belongs, and three people who can tell you why. Half the settlement's cleverness lives in this room.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Long benches, a high seat nobody sits in, and the charter nailed where the light falls on it. Read out loud once a season whether anyone asks for it or not.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Awnings, argument, and somebody's cousin selling salt at a price that is frankly insulting. Caravans stop here because it is worth stopping.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Hot stone, cold water, and the extravagance of spending either on being clean. Word of it travels further than word of the wall ever did.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low wall around the stone and a gate left open on purpose. Whatever is poured here is still gone by morning.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Raised to be seen from the road, and sited so that the road has to look. What is worshipped in it is the settlement's own business, and has changed at least once.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two registers of the same year kept on the same shelf, and a keeper who will show you both and let you decide. The disagreements are indexed.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Where the wall gives way, and the only place it does. Shut at dusk by somebody who has to be talked into opening it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The watch sleeps in shifts and eats together, which is why the watch is a thing and not a rota. Boots by the door in the order they came off.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stake driven into the ground, and a promise nailed to it: something is meant to rise here, as soon as the water and the hands can be spared.

part.Name: Chat
part.Says: [a design, chalked hastily beneath the notice.]

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cord and pegs marking out a rectangle of ground, and a tally of days scratched into the corner post. Something is being made here, a stage at a time.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A squared post sunk into cleared ground, waiting for a wall to be built against it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Rope-sprung and blanket-soft by local standards. It smells of road dust and relief.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Split logs worn smooth by sitting. The best arguments of the settlement happen here, and one or two of the marriages.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: An uncut stone with a cup-shaped hollow worn into its crown. Whatever is poured there is gone by morning, and no one asks where.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A cairn of fieldstone, raised for someone the settlement has not yet lost. It waits.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A salvaged cradle of chrome and gut-wire, cranked by whoever has the shift. Set your cells on it and go eat; they will be full when you come back.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A small stone marker, plain and unlettered. It says nothing about what stands around it - only that the keepers looked, and it was satisfied.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cut thornbrush lashed between stakes, taller than a man and meaner. It will not stop anyone determined. It will slow them down where your people can see them.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A platform on four legs with a bell and a good view of the road. The watch complains about the wind and never once about the posting.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Fieldstone laid without mortar, wide enough at the base to stand on. It took a season and everyone's back, and it will outlast everyone who built it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A thin codex in a plain wrapper, copied and recopied by people who had reason to. The margins argue with the text.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Hammered from tin and older promises, it holds just enough water to make strangers into kin. Whoever fills it and pours may found a place worth thirsting for.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A millstone yoked to a walking-bar. Three settlers lean into it from first light and spell each other at noon, and the shaft they turn runs under the packed floor to wherever the settlement wants the charge.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Paddles the settlement cut and lashed itself, standing in a race they dug under it and lined with clay. Nobody drinks out of that race. Somebody greases the shaft each morning and pulls the weed off the buckets. That is the whole of the work, and it is somebody's.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Four arms of brined wood and patched sailcloth on a post, trimmed by whoever draws the shift. On a still day it stands there being a landmark, and the settlement finds other work for the hands.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A jacketed pit of salt kept molten by the day's work and tapped after dark. The salt was already here. It is the one thing this country has never been short of.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Turned earth, wetted and trodden until it holds a shape. The cheapest wall anybody ever built, and the first one.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cut scrub, bound and left to ret. It becomes cord, thatch, and the canvas a tent is made of, and it is the reason a roof can go up in an afternoon.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A trunk stripped, squared, and stacked to season. Somebody spent a day on this with an axe.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Shale or limestone, split along the grain and dressed square. It was a hillside this morning.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Snails and coral on the geologic press, cut out of a seam somebody found and will not stop talking about.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Squared, planed, and true on every face. Half the trunk it came from went out of the saw-pit as dust.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Squared on the banker until every face meets every other at a right angle. It will sit where it is put for a thousand years.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Ruin-scrap taken back to liquid and poured into a mould. Somebody read the colour of the melt and knew when to tap it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A line of pegs and a cord, and a mark cut into the nearest thing still standing. Everything inside the cord is coming down, and the settlement will be the richer for it.

part.Name: Chat
part.Says: [a tally of what stands here, and what it is worth once it does not.]

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bare, level ground inside a staked square. Whatever stood here came down; whatever rises next can rise here again.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A notice on a stake, promising fresh water to whoever does what it asks.

part.Name: Chat
part.Says: [the price, and what it is for.]

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A short stake and a strip of cloth, the kind porters are trained to look for. Plant it on what you mean to have carried home, and walk on.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Pressed out of a windfall and dried on a cloth, still faintly sweet where the juice caught. Every one of them is a tree that has not happened yet.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Salt-crusted heads cut off a vine that had finished with them. They rattle. Put them in wet ground and stand back a week.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Damp grain run through with white thread, packed in a twist of bark. Not a seed at all, strictly; the people who sell it have never cared about the distinction.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A pressed disc of spore and ash the colour of something Qud has no word for. It is warm, and it should not be.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cut tops of tubers, each with a bud on it and a low note under it you feel in the jaw. Whoever cut them wore gloves and did not linger.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A young tree in a line of young trees, staked against a wind that has opinions. In a week there will be light in the branches.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Vine trained along a stake, its furrows still empty of salt. Somebody walks this row every morning with a bucket.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A raised bed of spent grain and shade, threaded white where the spawn took. It smells like rain in a cellar.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Spore-cake worked into cool soil and left alone. The keepers will not say what colour it comes up; the ones who have seen it do not have the word.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Shoots in a line, and under each one a swelling belly of tuber. Nobody sings while they weed this row.
